A campus map numbers its buildings and lists them in an index next to the
map, so a reader can find the library or the sports centre at a glance. 

This Stack Overflow question [Adding index to points in ggplot](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48869642/adding-index-to-points-in-ggplot)
shows such a map and asks how to draw the same kind of index in ggplot2,
noting that there is no built-in way.

The accepted answer is a workaround.

The same problem comes up in other questions, all quite old:
[numbered point labels plus a legend in a scatterplot](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24801987/numbered-point-labels-plus-a-legend-in-a-scatterplot) and [ggplot2: numbered points on plot and in legend](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57024684/ggplot2-numbered-points-on-plot-and-in-legend).

ggindex tries to solve this problem.

ggplot2 draws the numbers easily with `geom_text()` or `geom_label()`. 
The issue is to be able to draw the legend.

The examples below use the data from the question: five points, each with a
number and a description.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(ggindex)
```

```{r}
#| label: data
df <- data.frame(x = 6:10, y = 6:10, id = 1:5)
df$label <- paste0("Label", df$id)
```

## Numbers without a legend

`geom_label()` numbers the points, but nothing explains the numbers.

```{r}
#| label: label
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_label(aes(label = id), nudge_x = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Mapping the description to another aesthetic, such as `fill`, adds a legend.
Its keys show the point symbol, not the numbers, so the reader still can't
tell which point is which.

```{r}
#| label: fill
ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = label)) +
  geom_label(aes(label = id), nudge_x = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## The workaround: numbers in the legend text

The accepted answer pastes the number into the description, maps the result
to `fill` on an invisible layer, and hides the legend keys.

```{r}
#| label: workaround
df$legend <- paste0(df$id, ": ", df$label)

ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = legend), alpha = 0) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_label(aes(label = id), nudge_x = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_discrete(name = "Index") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(0, "cm"))
```

The result reads right, but the link between numbers and descriptions is
held together by hand:

- The legend is text only. The markers on the plot and in the legend don't
  match.
- The entries are sorted as text, so with ten or more points "10: ..."
  comes before "2: ...". Keeping the number order needs a factor with
  explicit levels.
- `fill` is used up by an invisible layer and can't show another variable.
- The numbers appear in two places, `id` and `legend`, which must be kept
  in sync.

## What ggindex adds

ggindex adds an `info` aesthetic with its own scale. Its legend keys draw the
marker with the `label` of each entry, so the numbers on the plot and in the
legend come from the same mapping.

```{r}
#| label: focus
ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = id, info = label)) +
  geom_focus() +
  scale_info_discrete("Index") +
  theme_minimal()
```

- Legend entries are sorted by `label`, as numbers.
- `colour` and `fill` style the markers and stay free for other variables.
- Without `label`, the `info` entries are numbered for you.
- `focus` numbers a subset of the points and leaves the rest to other
  layers.
- Maps work the same way with `geom_sf_focus()`.

See [Get started](ggindex.html) for these features,
[Styling numbered markers](styling.html) for colours, fonts, themes and facets,
and [Numbered markers on other plots](other-plots.html) for line charts, bar
charts and distributions.
